policy: Training data only; hyperparameters by GroupKFold (5 folds, shuffled groups, seed) on training run/engine IDs, scoring macro-F1, refit on all training rows; each panel scored once. Test labels only for scoring.

original_train.description: Tuned models trained only on the original revision-v3 training features (TEP late snapshots of 100 training runs; FD001 windows of 100 training engines) and scored on exactly the numeric features rendered in the LLM prompts. Like-for-like reference; hyperparameters by grouped CV.

legacy_untuned.description: Exact reproduction of the earlier untuned references (RF 300 trees, seed 20260926; StandardScaler + RBF SVM C=1, gamma=scale) on the original training features. Continuity check only.

tep_phase_aware.description: FAIR-TRANSFER (extra training information): original TEP late training rows plus the sample-40 snapshot (same definition as the early test panel) of the SAME 100 training runs for all 7 classes, i.e. labelled examples of the early phase. Run-disjoint from every test panel.

fd002_in_domain_raw.description: FAIR-TRANSFER (extra training information): labelled FD002 training engines (official train_FD002, disjoint partition from the 60 test engines). Same 60-feature 30-cycle summary as the LLM, no regime normalization. Balanced sampled cut points (see training_design).

fd002_in_domain_regime_norm.description: FAIR-TRANSFER (extra training information + different features): as fd002_in_domain_raw, but every sensor is z-scored per operating regime (KMeans, 6 regimes, fitted on train_FD002 settings) before computing the same 30-cycle summaries. Test features are transformed the same way, so they are NOT the numbers the LLM saw.

fd001_regime_norm_transfer.description: FAIR-TRANSFER (unlabelled target statistics + different features): classifier trained only on FD001 labels (FD001 z-scored with its own training statistics, one regime). FD002 test engines are normalized with per-regime statistics estimated from UNLABELLED train_FD002 sensor data (no RUL used). Also scored on the FD001 panel (same normalization) as an in-domain check.

tep_late.description: 70 new TEP runs (10/class), late snapshot at a seeded sample in [200,500] (independent validation, LLM condition 'clean').

tep_early.description: Same 70 runs at sample 40 (~60 min after fault injection) (independent validation, LLM condition 'early').

tep_v3.description: Original revision-v3 TEP held-out panel: 70 runs (10/class), late snapshot.

fd001_v3.description: Original revision-v3 FD001 held-out panel: 60 official test engines (20/RUL class), last 30 cycles.

fd002.description: 60 FD002 official test engines (20/RUL class), last 30 cycles, FD001 feature representation (LLM condition 'fd002').

pipelines.HGB: HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=200, early_stopping=False) (gradient-boosting reference in place of XGBoost)

methods.grid_note: class_weight is searched only when training classes are imbalanced (max/min > 1.2: FD001 only). Ties broken by first candidate in grid order (defaults first).

tep_phase_aware.sampling: All 7 classes x the 100 revision-v3 training runs at sample 40 (fault injected after sample 20; 3-minute sampling), 4-decimal rounding as in the prompts. Appended to the 2100 late training rows; CV groups = run ID shared across classes.

fd002.sampling: Balanced labelled windows from train_FD002 run-to-failure trajectories. For every training engine and every RUL class, FD002_CUTS_PER_CLASS observation endpoints are drawn without replacement (fixed seed) among those with a complete 30-cycle past window whose RUL (= failure cycle - endpoint cycle) falls into the class. Bins match the test panel: Healthy RUL>80, Degrading 30<RUL<=80, Critical RUL<=30. The FD002 test panel is balanced (20/20/20), so classes are balanced by construction.

regime_normalization.method: Operating-regime-wise sensor standardization, standard in the C-MAPSS literature. Regimes are KMeans clusters of the three standardized operating settings (raw columns 2-4), fitted on training rows only; every sensor (columns 5-25) is then z-scored with the training mean/std of its regime. With one regime this reduces to global per-sensor standardization (FD001 has a single condition).
regime_normalization.fd001: Single regime: global per-sensor standardization with train_FD001 statistics.

sanity_checks.fd002_partition_note: train_FD002 and test_FD002 are distinct official partitions; numeric engine IDs are namespaced by partition and denote different engines. Verified additionally by zero raw-row overlap.
